prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: Buchwald-Hartwig amination is the clearest example on the shortlist of a general method that changed how chemists everywhere build bonds: ligand-controlled Pd catalysis turned aryl C-N formation from a narrow, harsh reaction into a routine step in medicinal and process chemistry, with a clear mechanistic basis and three decades of independent use. Pairing it with base editing gives a prize that spans molecule-making and chemical biology. In base editing the new chemistry is concrete: a deaminase is brought to a defined single-stranded DNA window by a programmable nickase, and the adenine editor required directed evolution of a deaminase that does not exist in nature. Liu alone keeps the combined prize at three names and avoids the Komor/Gaudelli versus Nishida/Kondo allocation problem.
statement.case_against: My first-ranked candidate was ranked by only four members and placed sixth to eighth by three of them, mainly because it extends the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize and may look incremental. The combination is also a two-part prize that gives no weight to the targeted protein degradation candidate that most of my colleagues rank first. Base editing sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize, and its clinical record is still short. Choosing it for its deaminase chemistry is defensible but is not a consensus view.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks C-N coupling sixth and says it is vast in impact but an extension of a field already recognised in 2010; he also finds the Buchwald/Hartwig pair clean.
responses.response: I agree on the pair and the impact. I disagree that 2010 should count heavily against it. Negishi, Suzuki and Heck were C-C couplings, and C-N and C-O bond formation needed different ligand design and mechanistic insight, notably oxidative addition followed by amide binding and C-N reductive elimination. The two sets of reactions solve different problems for the working chemist. The 2010 precedent is a legitimate concern, but I do not think it answers the question of what was new.

responses.point: Linke ranks Pd C-N coupling last, calls it possibly an incremental extension of the 2010 prize, and suggests Kosugi be included to reflect precedent.
responses.response: I do not think Kosugi belongs in the prize. His tin-amide coupling needed stoichiometric tin reagents and was narrow in scope. The general catalytic amination with ligand-controlled scope came from Buchwald and Hartwig, so including him would obscure that. On the incrementalism point I would ask for the data: how many drug syntheses and process routes use this reaction, rather than whether the headline sounds like 2010.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first and values the defined deaminase chemistry, while noting that Komor and Gaudelli are natural co-credits and Kondo and Nishida ran parallel work.
responses.response: I share the chemical argument for B042 and have moved it up in my thinking, although I would still limit the credit to Liu. Komor and Gaudelli were the lead authors, but the invention of the architecture, and the directed evolution of the adenine deaminase, came from one group. This also keeps a combined prize within three. I accept that leaving out Kondo and Nishida is a real weakness, and I would like to see their timeline against Komor's 2016 paper.

responses.point: Zou ranks PROTACs first, treating the PROTAC concept and the cereblon mechanism as two distinct pillars that three names cannot cover fairly.
responses.response: I agree that the credit problem is the central obstacle for B014: Crews, Deshaies and Handa/Ito would each have a different discovery. As a synthetic chemist I am less moved by the concept than by what ends up as a general method others can use. I will keep B014 as my first alternative, but I would want the committee to decide whether the prize honours the PROTAC concept or the glue mechanism before it is proposed.

uncertainties: Whether the committee sees Pd C-N coupling as distinct enough from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
How the committee treats Kondo and Nishida relative to Liu on base editing.
Whether a two-part prize is acceptable when the first part has weak opening support.
How much clinical evidence for degraders or base editors the committee needs before recognition.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr, which is not a recusal matter for the candidates on the shortlist; none of the credited individuals is a known collaborator or former mentor.
